description: Table 4 is a single, full-width comparison table (rendered as an image) with no micrographs or curves. It has a four-column layout: a leftmost row-label column headed "Mechanism", then one column for each of three deformation mechanisms — "SIP [6]", "MBIP [74]" and "DSBR [85]". Eleven row headers run down the left column: Character, Alloy composition, Solution treatment, Cooling rate, As quenched microstructure, γ grain size, SFE, Tensile sample, Strain rate, UTS/TE (the mechanism and row-label header share the top band). The table's scientific role is to show that the three proposed plasticity mechanisms for high-Al, high-SFE austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels were established on distinctly different alloys and testing conditions, so their strain-hardening behaviour is not directly comparable: compositions range from Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C (SIP) through Fe-28Mn-10Al-1.0C (MBIP) to Fe-30.4Mn-8Al-1.2C (DSBR); solution treatments from 1050 °C/25 min to 1000 °C/60 min and 1100 °C/120 min; cooling by water quenching (SIP, MBIP) versus oil quenching (DSBR); as-quenched microstructures of γ + 8% δ + κ′ (20–30 nm) for SIP versus γ + SRO (<2 nm) for MBIP and DSBR; γ grain sizes of ~30, 64 and 40 μm; SFE of 110, 120 and 85 mJ/m²; strain rates of 10⁻⁴, 10⁻³ and 5 × 10⁻⁴ /s; and UTS/TE of 875 MPa/58%, 873 MPa/98.9% and 900 MPa/68%. Every cell is printed and legible.

observations.observation: Table 4 compares three deformation mechanisms of high-Al austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels, labelled SIP [6], MBIP [74] and DSBR [85].
The alloy compositions tabulated are Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C (SIP), Fe-28Mn-10Al-1.0C (MBIP) and Fe-30.4Mn-8Al-1.2C (DSBR).
Solution treatments are 1050 °C/25 min (SIP), 1000 °C/60 min (MBIP) and 1100 °C/120 min (DSBR), with water quenching for SIP and MBIP and oil quenching for DSBR.
As-quenched microstructures are printed as 'γ + 8% δ + κ′ (20–30 nm)' for SIP and 'γ + SRO (<2 nm)' for both MBIP and DSBR.
γ grain sizes are ~30 μm (SIP), 64 μm (MBIP) and 40 μm (DSBR).
Stacking fault energies are 110 mJ/m2 (SIP), 120 mJ/m2 (MBIP) and 85 mJ/m2 (DSBR).
UTS/TE values are 875 MPa/58% (SIP), 873 MPa/98.9% (MBIP) and 900 MPa/68% (DSBR).
Tensile sample geometries are 'Specimen not reported 1 mm thickness' (SIP), 25.4 mm × 6 mm × 2 mm (MBIP) and 40 mm × diameter 6 mm (DSBR).

The characters listed are: homogenous shear band formation sustained by nano sized κ′-carbides (SIP), grain subdivision by microband intersections (MBIP), and grain refinement of slip band structure (DSBR).
The caption states that Table 4 is 'The comparison of the experimental conditions for three deformation mechanisms'.
The citing text states that the steel compositions, process parameters and microstructures for these alloys are summarized in Table 4.

The citing text states MBIP and DSBR were observed in austenite where SROs are present, while SIP was observed in austenite where the κ′-carbides already exist, matching the as-quenched microstructures in the table.
The three mechanisms correspond to different alloy compositions, grain sizes and SFE values, so their strain-hardening data are not obtained on a single reference alloy.
